facts.statement: Within the Troodontidae, the closest relative of Liaoningvenator was Eosinopteryx, and it was also closely related to Anchiornis and Xiaotingia.

facts.statement: Liaoningvenator was a small troodontid with an estimated total body length of approximately 69 cm.
facts.quote: With a total body length (estimated lengths of the skull, neck, trunk, and tail combined) of approximately 69 cm, Liaoningvenator is a small troodontid.

facts.statement: Liaoningvenator possessed a long, narrow, and triangular skull measuring 9.8 cm in length.
facts.quote: Liaoningvenator possesses a long, narrow, and triangular skull that measured 9.8 cm long.

facts.statement: The maxilla of Liaoningvenator had three openings: the premaxillary, maxillary, and antorbital fenestrae.
facts.quote: There are three openings on the surface of the maxilla, the premaxillary, maxillary, and antorbital fenestrae.

facts.statement: Uniquely among troodontids, the postorbital bone of Liaoningvenator was slender and radiated into three processes.
facts.quote: Uniquely among troodontids, the postorbital bone is slender and radiates into three processes.

facts.statement: The teeth at the rear of the lower jaw of Liaoningvenator were serrated, unlike in many basal troodontids.
facts.quote: The teeth towards the rear of the lower jaw are serrated, unlike a number of basal troodontids.

facts.statement: Liaoningvenator had ten cervical vertebrae, twelve dorsal vertebrae, and at least sixteen caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: There are ten cervical vertebrae, twelve dorsal (trunk) vertebrae, and at least sixteen caudal (tail) vertebrae in Liaoningvenator.

facts.statement: In Liaoningvenator, the transition point where the tail vertebrae became sub-triangular occurred at the seventh caudal vertebra, which is further forward than in Sinornithoides and Mei.
facts.quote: In the tail, the transition point - the point where the sides of the caudals become more compressed such that they are sub-triangular instead of rectangular - occurs at the seventh caudal, further forward than Sinornithoides and Mei (where it occurs at the ninth).

facts.statement: On the humerus of Liaoningvenator, the deltopectoral crest extended for 40% of the bone's length and terminated halfway down the bone.
facts.quote: On the humerus, the deltopectoral crest extends for 40% of the bone's length, and terminates halfway down the bone.

facts.statement: The humerus of Liaoningvenator was 59% the length of the femur, which is shorter relative to the femur than in Eosinopteryx (80% length).
facts.quote: The humerus is shorter, relative to the femur, in Liaoningvenator (59% length) than in Eosinopteryx (80% length).

facts.statement: In Liaoningvenator, the first phalanx of the first digit of the hand was 1.49 times the length of the second metacarpal, a unique trait among three-digited hands.
facts.quote: Further below, the three-digited hand is unique in that the first phalanx of the first digit is longer than the second metacarpal, at 1.49 times the length of the latter.

facts.statement: The hindlimb of Liaoningvenator was twice the length of its torso, whereas in Mei it was 2.8 times the length of the torso.
facts.quote: The hindlimb of Liaoningvenator is twice the length of the torso, while in Mei it is 2.8 times the length of the torso.

facts.statement: Unlike Sinovenator, Liaoningvenator possessed a fourth trochanter on its femur.
facts.quote: Unlike Sinovenator, Liaoningvenator has a fourth trochanter on its femur.

facts.statement: The four-digited foot of Liaoningvenator was highly compacted with a tarsus that narrowed toward the bottom.
facts.quote: The four-digited foot is highly compacted, with a tarsus that narrows toward the bottom.

facts.statement: The Liaoningvenator specimen was found in the Lujiatun Beds of the Yixian Formation in Shangyuan, Beipiao, Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: It was found in the Lujiatun Beds of the Yixian Formation in Shangyuan, Beipiao, Liaoning, China

facts.statement: The Liaoningvenator specimen is currently stored at the Dalian Natural History Museum under the accession number DNHM D3012.
facts.quote: currently, it is stored at the Dalian Natural History Museum (DNHM) in Dalian, Liaoning under the accession number DNHM D3012.

facts.statement: The Liaoningvenator specimen was found with its head curved forward and limbs tucked in, differing from the classic death pose and the sleeping postures of Mei and Sinornithoides.
facts.quote: Its head is curved forward, and its limbs are tucked in; this differs from both the classic death pose (where the head is flexed backwards), as well as the sleeping posture of Mei and Sinornithoides.

facts.statement: The genus name Liaoningvenator combines "Liaoning" with the Latin suffix -venator, meaning "hunter".
facts.quote: The genus name Liaoningvenator combines Liaoning with the suffix -venator, meaning "hunter" in Latin

facts.statement: The pneumatic opening on the rear of the quadrate and the oval shape of the foramen magnum helped identify Liaoningvenator as a troodontid.
facts.quote: the pneumatic opening on the rear of its quadrate; the oval shape of its foramen magnum

facts.statement: Shallow midline grooves replacing neural spines in the vertebrae towards the end of the tail were key features used to classify Liaoningvenator.
facts.quote: the replacement of neural spines by shallow midline grooves in the vertebrae towards the end of its tail

facts.statement: A tall ascending process on the astragalus was one of the characteristics used to place Liaoningvenator within the Troodontidae.
facts.quote: the tall ascending process on its astragalus

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis by Shen and colleagues found that Liaoningvenator formed a clade with Eosinopteryx, Anchiornis, and Xiaotingia.
facts.quote: Shen and colleagues found that Liaoningvenator formed a unified group, or clade, with Eosinopteryx, Anchiornis, and Xiaotingia

facts.statement: The grouping of Liaoningvenator with Anchiornis and Xiaotingia offered evidence against their traditional placement as non-troodontid members of the Paraves.
facts.quote: thus offering contrary evidence to the traditional placement of these taxa as non-troodontid members of the Paraves

facts.statement: The genus name Liaoningvenator combines Liaoning with the Latin suffix -venator meaning 'hunter', while the specific name curriei honors Canadian paleontologist Philip John Currie.

facts.statement: Liaoningvenator's skeleton had an exceptional posture with its head curved forward and limbs tucked, differing from the classic death pose or sleeping posture seen in Mei and Sinornithoides.

facts.statement: The presence of avascular bone in outer layers and evidence of bone remodeling suggest the holotype was nearing skeletal maturity.

facts.statement: Shen and colleagues identified Liaoningvenator as one of eleven known troodontids from China and the fifth early Cretaceous Chinese troodontid.
facts.quote: Según Shen y colegas, Liaoningvenator es uno de los once trodóntidos conocidos de China y el quinto troodontido chino del Cretácico temprano después de Sinovenator , Sinusonasus , Mei y Jinfengopteryx .

facts.quote: Mientras Shen y sus colegas asignaron las camas Lujiatun al Hauteriviense, las estimaciones de fechas más recientes publicadas por Chang Su-chin y sus colegas sugirieron una edad más joven de alrededor de 126 millones de años para las camas Lujiatun, que data de la época Barremiense.

facts.statement: The Lujiatun beds consist of fluvial and volcanic deposits, indicating a landscape of rivers and volcanoes that may have killed the animals via lahars.
facts.quote: Los lechos de Lujiatun consisten en depósitos fluviales y volcánicos, lo que indica un paisaje de ríos con volcanes, que pudo haber matado a los animales preservados por lahar.

facts.statement: The average annual air temperature in the region where Liaoningvenator lived reached a minimum of 10 degrees Celsius.
